chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:
[48:4] He it is Who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the Momineen
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic:'
[58:22] and He has Supported them with a Spirit from Him
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the iman (faith).'

key_terms.أَيَّدَهُمْ: ayyada-hum (He supported them) — divine reinforcement and strengthening of the believers through the Spirit
key_terms.السَّكِينَةَ: sakina (tranquility) — the divine calm and serenity sent into the hearts of the believers, interpreted by the Imam as iman
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: iman (faith) — the inner reality of belief, identified as the substance of both the sakina and the supporting Spirit
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Momineen (believers) — those whose hearts are the locus of the divinely sent tranquility
key_terms.رُوحٍ: ruh (Spirit) — the divine Spirit with which Allah supports the believers, interpreted as iman
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Azza wa Jall (Mighty and Majestic) — the honorific for Allah affirming His absolute power and transcendence
key_terms.قُلُوبِ: qulub (hearts) — the spiritual center of the human being, the vessel and receptacle of divine tranquility

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the tranquility sent down into the hearts of the believers' (Quran 48:4) and 'the Spirit from Him' (Quran 58:22) according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) interprets two Quranic verses — 48:4, concerning the sakina (tranquility) sent down into the hearts of the believers, and 58:22, concerning the Spirit with which Allah supports the believers — by identifying both as referring to iman (faith). This hadith establishes that the divine gifts of tranquility and spiritual support are not distinct metaphysical entities separate from faith, but are essential manifestations of iman itself, grounding two major Quranic theological concepts in the inner reality of belief.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [48:4] He it is Who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the Momineen (plural of Momin).
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [58:22] and He has Supported them with a Spirit from Him.
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is the faith’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Hamza from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘He sent down serenity into the hearts of the believers. . . [48:4] The Imam said, ‘It (serenity) is belief.’
I (the narrator) then asked him about the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘He supported them with a spirit from Him. . . .’
[58:22] The Imam said, ‘It (spirit) is belief.’”
